# Data sources and connections {#data-sources}

The package keeps no copies of its own. Each function goes to the original
source, reads only the part it needs and caches whatever can be reused later.

| Source | Product | Coverage | Resolution | Reference | Access | Functions |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| MapBiomas | Collection 10, tiles | Brazil | 30 m | 1985–2024 | Bioma Stats API → file list per tile → GeoTIFF | `load_rasters(method = "download")` |
| MapBiomas | Collection 10, national map | Brazil | 30 m | 1985–2024 | annual GeoTIFF from the public MapBiomas repository (~28 GB, 40 years) | `download_mapbiomas()`, `load_rasters(method = "library")` |
| ESA | WorldCover | world | 10 m | 2020 (v100), 2021 (v200) | Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF over HTTP | `load_lulc()` |
| Copernicus / ESA | DEM GLO-30 | world | 30 m | 2011–2015 | Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF over HTTP | `load_physical()` |
| ISRIC | SoilGrids 2.0 | world | 250 m | 2021 | WCS service, area subset only | `load_physical()` |
| OpenStreetMap | Regional extracts (Geofabrik, openstreetmap.fr) | world | vector | extract date | `.osm.pbf` file with local cache | `load_features(source = "osm")` |
| Overture Maps | GeoParquet | world | vector | release | STAC index and partial reads from S3 | `load_features(source = "overture")` |

As for licences, MapBiomas uses CC BY-SA; ESA WorldCover and SoilGrids, CC BY
4.0; Copernicus DEM, the free Copernicus licence; OpenStreetMap, ODbL; and
Overture, ODbL and CDLA. Please cite the sources you use when publishing
results.

`layer_catalog()` returns this same list for the external layers and, with
`online = TRUE`, checks whether each server is responding.

## Connections, failures and cache {-}

For selective downloads, the package queries the **Bioma Stats API**
(`api.biomastats.org`, with a backup mirror) to find out which files make up
each tile. That list is cached for 7 days, and maps that were already
downloaded are reused in later runs.

**External layers** have a 5-second time limit. If a source does not respond in
time, fails or refuses access, it is set aside: the function returns that block
with status `"skipped"` and carries on with the others, without stopping the
analysis. On slow connections, the limit can be raised with
`options(biomastats.timeout = 10)`.

Extracts, indexes and file lists are kept in the user **cache**
(`tools::R_user_dir("biomastats", "cache")`). Interrupted downloads leave no
partial files behind.

::: {.nota}
Institutions with their own mirrors can point the package to them, for example
with `options(biomastats.worldcover_root = "https://...")`. The options
`biomastats.copernicus_root`, `biomastats.soilgrids_wcs` and
`biomastats.overture_stac` are also available.
:::
